description: Shared baseline (identical across the maintainer's repositories; the only differences are dependencyDashboard and the packageRules at the end whose description starts with "Repo-specific:"). Auto-merge is limited to the dev tooling group: Renovate merges it itself once CI is green and the 3-day release age has passed (platformAutomerge is off, so it works without GitHub auto-merge or branch protection). Everything that ships to production waits for a human.

packageRules.description: Group dev tooling + types — auto-merge if CI is green
@types/node follows the Node 24 runtime, not npm's latest tag
Group framework deps — single PR, manual review (a superset: packages a repo does not use simply never match)
Major bumps always get their own PR, never auto-merge
Pin GitHub Actions to commit SHAs (security best practice)

engines (node/npm) are floors, not versions to track: npm >= 11.10 is what the min-release-age gate needs, and the runtime Node version is pinned by the Dockerfile image and CI's NODE_VERSION, so a bare major is on purpose. Bumping them to the newest release breaks CI's engine-strict install (EBADENGINE).
packageManager documents the npm bundled with the pinned Node; it moves with Node, not on its own (CI uses the bundled npm).
Node: CI's NODE_VERSION and the Docker node image (where there is one) move together in one PR, so production runs what CI tested; never auto-merged.
Repo-specific: WXT, its modules and postcss shape the shipped extension bundle, so they join the framework group (single PR, manual review)
Repo-specific: axe's Playwright binding is dev tooling like axe-core and Playwright, so it joins that group

customManagers.description: CI's NODE_VERSION env, grouped with the Docker node image by the node rule
